_comment: Short 2 in docs/CONTENT.md — the January reset. The first line is carried in `variants` because tts.mjs treats that as the hook; here the hook IS the first thing drawn.
_injury: Slipped on ice, which is also why it is January. House style: the injury has to earn its place in the story, not just be different from the last one.
_numbers: A $1,000 deductible and the SAME $400 visit in both months — that is the whole point. What changes is the split: $100 you / $300 insurance in November, $400 you / $0 insurance in January. An earlier cut showed $40 against $400 as though the PRICE had changed, which is the exact confusion this Short exists to undo. Deliberately not $800, which is Short 1's number; reusing figures across Shorts implies a connection that is not there.
_jargon: The word 'deductible' is withheld until the second-to-last line, on purpose. The bucket is explained first and named afterwards, so a viewer who has never heard the word still understands the mechanism before it arrives.

variants.ice: Your body does not know it is January. Your insurance does.

body.text: Every year you pay the first chunk of your own care. Here, the first thousand dollars.
By November you had filled it.
So when you went in, the hospital billed four hundred.
You paid one hundred of it. Your insurance paid the other three hundred.
Then on the first of January, they tip it out.
Same knee, same clinic, same four hundred dollar bill.
This time you pay all four hundred, and your insurance pays nothing.
The word for that bucket is deductible. This one is a thousand dollars a year. Yours will be a different number.
Check yours before you dispute. Or upload them free at UseClaimRight.com.
